speakers.name: Dame Nia Griffith
speakers.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Wales

contributions.text: 9. What discussions she has had with the Welsh Government on school standards in Wales.
contributions.name: Sir Ashley Fox

contributions.who: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Wales (Dame Nia Griffith)
contributions.text: The UK Government have delivered the biggest Budget settlement in the history of devolution, with £21 billion of new money for the Welsh Government. The Welsh Government are investing almost £200 million this year to support school standards across Wales, plus a further almost £170 million next year. The hon. Member’s Welsh Conservative colleagues tried to block that funding by voting against the Welsh Government Budget last week.
contributions.name: Dame Nia Griffith
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Wales

contributions.text: Children in Wales have the lowest PISA —programme for international student assessment— scores in the United Kingdom and are significantly below the OECD average. Does the Minister believe that that could be related to 26 years of Labour government in Wales?
contributions.name: Sir Ashley Fox

contributions.text: I will take no lectures from the Conservatives. Their attacks ring hollow given the chronic underfunding of education and public services over the 14 years they were in power. Now, the UK and Welsh Governments are working together to ensure that every young person has the opportunity to succeed, by investing over £260 million extra in education and more than £260 million in local government, which sets school budgets in Wales. In spite of the shenanigans of Plaid and the Conservatives voting against the Welsh Government’s Budget, Labour is getting on and delivering certainty and support for teachers across Wales through increases to education and local authority budgets.
contributions.name: Dame Nia Griffith
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Wales

contributions.text: Does my hon. Friend welcome, as I do, the additional £20 million announced by the Welsh Government last week to improve education standards, on top of the £262 million extra in total for education in Wales? Is she as perplexed as I am as to why the Conservatives and Plaid Cymru voted against extra money for education in the Welsh budget?
contributions.name: Gill German

contributions.text: Like my hon. Friend, I am absolutely astounded by the way that Plaid Cymru and Conservative Senedd Members voted against the budget, but the important thing is that this year the Welsh Government will be investing an additional £1.1 million in literacy, numeracy and science support in schools. The Welsh Government have also announced a £10 million investment package for literacy and numeracy in the coming year, increasing local capacity to support schools, national support programmes and interventions to support budding learners.
contributions.name: Dame Nia Griffith
contributions.role: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Wales
